title: Bian Que and Duke Huan of Cai
text:
The legendary physician Bian Que came to see Duke Huan of Cai. After standing before him for a while, he said: "My lord, you have an illness in the skin. If it is not treated, it will go deeper." The duke replied that he was perfectly well. When Bian Que left, the duke remarked that doctors like to treat healthy people so they can take credit for curing them.

Ten days later Bian Que came again and said the illness had reached the flesh. The duke did not answer and was displeased. Ten days after that Bian Que said it had reached the stomach and intestines. Again the duke ignored him.

After another ten days, Bian Que caught sight of the duke, turned and walked away. The duke sent someone to ask why. Bian Que explained that an illness in the skin can be reached with poultices, in the flesh with needles, and in the stomach with herbal broths. But now it was in the marrow of the bones, where it belonged to the god of fate, and nothing could be done, so he had nothing more to say.

Five days later the duke felt pain all through his body. He sent for Bian Que, who had already fled to the state of Qin. The duke died.
lesson: Problems are cheapest to fix when they are still small and easy to deny. Listen most carefully to the warnings that arrive while you still feel fine.
people: Bian Que, Duke Huan of Cai
source: Han Feizi, Yu Lao (Illustrations of Laozi)
caveat: Bian Que is a semi-legendary figure, and the Shiji tells a similar story with a duke of Qi.
